cards.title: Audit algorithmic visibility with unbranded LLM prompts
cards.summary: Test whether ChatGPT, Perplexity and similar AI platforms recommend your store for unbranded category queries, the way early SEO audits tested Google rankings.
cards.use_when: You want to diagnose whether your store is invisible to AI-driven product discovery, or benchmark visibility before investing in an AI-search strategy.
steps: List the unbranded questions your ideal customer would actually ask an AI assistant (e.g. 'best budget running shoes for flat feet', 'where to buy organic dog food online'), covering your main categories, price tiers and use cases.
Run each prompt repeatedly across multiple LLMs you care about (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini) and record which brands get named, what order, and whether you appear at all.
Repeat the runs on different days, because results vary between sessions and the systems are partly a black box; treat any single run as a noisy signal rather than a fixed ranking.
Note which sources the models appear to lean on when they name competitors (review sites, forums, retailer listings, press) so you know which third-party surfaces to influence.
Re-run the same prompt set periodically as a visibility tracker, the equivalent of rank tracking, and tie changes back to PR, review-generation or content pushes you made.
Set a decision rule internally: if even a meaningful minority of your audience starts searches on AI platforms, invisibility there is a revenue risk worth budget.
caveats: The presenter reports getting completely different rankings across industries and runs; LLM answers are non-deterministic, so don't treat a single test as definitive.
Minority of consumers currently search and buy this way; the source expects this to grow fast but gives no measured adoption data.

cards.title: Win LLM recommendations by engineering third-party customer content
cards.summary: Third-party content — especially customers speaking positively about your brand — is the strongest observed influence on whether LLMs recommend you, so shift discoverability effort toward review and mention generation.
cards.use_when: You are planning acquisition and brand-discovery investment and deciding how to allocate SEO/content budget toward AI platforms rather than only Google.
steps: Inventory where your brand is already discussed by third parties: review platforms, forums, community threads, comparison articles, press and creator content.
Prioritize generating genuine positive customer mentions over polishing your own site copy, because the source observes customer feedback as the biggest influence on LLM recommendations today.
Build systematic review collection into post-purchase flows (thank-you pages, email, packaging inserts) so volume and recency of third-party reviews keeps growing.
Encourage customers to describe specific use cases and outcomes in reviews, since unstructured but detailed mentions give models more to retrieve and cite.
Seed or support presence in the communities and comparison sites the models seem to reference during your visibility audit, without faking reviews.
Measure impact by re-running your unbranded LLM prompt audit over time and watching whether you start appearing in answers.
caveats: The source calls the ranking mechanism a black box; the third-party-content signal is an observation, not a documented ranking factor.
Today LLM recommendations are described as not advertising-biased, but the presenter expects that could change.
Fabricated reviews breach platform rules and undermine the trust signal you are trying to build.

cards.title: Redesign the funnel for AI platforms where inspiration, comparison and checkout happen together
cards.summary: If AI platforms collapse the whole funnel — inspiration, filtering and purchase — into one surface, your go-to-market plan must work inside that surface, not only across your own site and ads.
cards.use_when: You are setting next-year acquisition and go-to-market strategy and need to decide whether and how to sell or be discovered inside AI assistants.
steps: Map your current funnel stages (awareness, consideration, purchase, support) and mark which ones a customer can already complete inside an AI platform rather than on your site.

Check whether the major AI platforms your customers use now support in-platform purchasing or app integrations, and verify the current merchant or app-listing requirements directly with each platform, since interfaces change quickly.
Ensure product data, pricing, availability and brand personality are represented in whatever structured form these platforms consume, so an agent can present and transact accurately.
Decide your stance on in-platform checkout versus driving traffic back to your own store; weigh margin, data ownership and convenience against each other rather than assuming one model wins.

Prepare a trigger for action: the source suggests a realistic near-term scenario where a significant share of customers, on the order of 10-20%, use this flow, which would justify a full go-to-market rethink.
Reassess quarterly, because the source expects the environment to look materially different within roughly a year.
caveats: The presenter notes this is currently a minority of customers and still not fully convenient.
The 10-20% adoption figure is the presenter's forward-looking heuristic, not measured data.

cards.title: Prepare for price pressure from zero-effort consumer shopping agents
cards.summary: When consumers outsource deal-hunting to personal agents that monitor and rebuy automatically, search effort and price loyalty drop, squeezing ecommerce margins.
cards.use_when: You are setting pricing, promotion or differentiation strategy and want to stress-test how your offer survives agent-driven comparison shopping.
steps: Accept the mechanism the source describes: consumers can deploy agents that monitor a purchased item and automatically cancel and rebook when the price falls roughly 10% below what they paid, with near-zero effort.
Assume that over time a meaningful segment of buyers will let agents find the cheapest acceptable option in the background, reducing the friction that currently protects your price.
Stress-test your catalog: for each product, ask whether it would survive pure price comparison once a buyer's agent can scan the market at no cost.
Shift defensibility toward things agents can't trivially price-match: exclusive or private-label products, bundles, service level, membership, community and post-purchase experience.
Audit subscription and replenishment pricing against the risk that agents auto-switch customers to cheaper alternatives the moment better terms appear.
Consider whether your own store should offer agent-friendly integrations or price-match logic, and weigh that against margin erosion.
caveats: This is a forward-looking prediction, not an observed mass behavior today; current agent adoption is limited.
The ~10% repricing trigger is the presenter's illustrative example, not a benchmark to build a pricing rule on.

cards.title: Turn support interactions into a profit center with context-aware upselling
cards.summary: AI-driven support can cut cost per contact toward zero while high-context, non-intrusive recommendations raise return per contact, converting a cost center into a profit center.
cards.use_when: You are designing post-purchase support automation and want to decide whether and how to add upselling or cross-selling into service interactions.
steps: Establish baseline metrics separately: cost per contact (automation efficiency) and return per contact (revenue generated during support), so you can prove the shift rather than assume it.
Give support agents or bots a complete, accurate view of the customer's history, order and context, because the source ties upsell accuracy directly to how well the system knows the customer.
Resolve the customer's issue first, then surface a relevant recommendation; the source argues appreciation and acceptance are higher when context is accurate and the suggestion is not intrusive.
Automate high-volume, low-complexity contacts to push cost per contact down while keeping humans available for emotional or complex cases.
Train the recommendation logic on what genuinely fits that customer rather than generic best-sellers, and monitor acceptance and complaint rates to catch intrusive behavior.
Track the ratio over time: falling cost per contact plus rising return per contact is the signal that the cost center has flipped to a profit center.
caveats: This is a prediction about an emerging capability, not a documented result; validate with your own controlled tests.
Upselling in a support moment can damage trust if it feels opportunistic; keep it contextual and optional.
The source gives no measured cost-per-contact or upsell-lift figures.

cards.title: Build hyperpersonalization as a 24/7 coaching assistant, not just marketing copy
cards.summary: Move hyperpersonalization beyond personalized messaging toward an always-available expert assistant that delivers ongoing value using the brand's category expertise.
cards.use_when: You are planning post-purchase retention and loyalty features and deciding whether to build a personalized assistant or coach for customers.
steps: Identify where your brand holds genuine category expertise that customers need advice on repeatedly after purchase (beauty routines, training plans, cooking, product usage).
Design an assistant around that expertise, following the source's L'Oreal example: a beauty assistant that answers hair, skin and nail questions as an always-on coach.
Scope it around customer value rather than campaign messaging; the source explicitly argues most organizations limit hyperpersonalization to communications and miss the larger opportunity.
Tie the assistant to post-purchase moments — setup, usage, troubleshooting, replenishment — so it deepens the relationship over the product's life rather than only at acquisition.
Feed it the customer's own order history and preferences so advice is specific, and make opt-in and data use clear.
Measure retention, repeat purchase and engagement rather than just chat volume, since the goal is personalized value delivered over time.
caveats: Source example is L'Oreal's beauty assistant; do not assume unproven revenue outcomes for your own build.
An assistant that gives weak or generic advice can degrade trust more than no assistant at all.

cards.title: Add an emotional-value layer to AI projects beyond efficiency
cards.summary: The source argues AI has been used mostly for efficiency, while the biggest untapped use is emotional value — inspiration, delight and personal growth — which can differentiate the brand.
cards.use_when: You are prioritizing an AI roadmap and want to choose post-purchase or brand-experience projects that create emotional rather than purely operational value.
steps: List current AI initiatives and label each as efficiency (faster, cheaper, 24/7) or emotional (inspires, delights, supports the customer personally).
Deliberately fund at least one emotional project, since the source claims the efficiency ground is crowded and emotional applications are a blue ocean.
Look for customer moments where emotional support is relevant: styling for an event, accessibility features, personal milestones, product-use inspiration.

Use examples the source cites as direction, not as templates to copy: smart glasses with automated subtitles for deaf users, or an app like Ralph Lauren's 'Talk to Ralph' offering party-outfit inspiration.
Validate emotional features with qualitative feedback and loyalty signals, not just support-cost metrics.
Keep the initiative tied to your brand's expertise and voice so emotional AI feels like your brand, not a generic assistant.
caveats: The source references a study suggesting companionship and emotion are a top use of generative AI; do not overgeneralize it to purchase behavior.
Building emotional features is speculative and costly; the source gives no proven ROI.

cards.title: Offer belonging as a service through human community
cards.summary: As AI-perfect service becomes a commodity, the source predicts brands that facilitate real human community will differentiate — belonging becomes a service, not a nice-to-have.
cards.use_when: You are planning retention and loyalty strategy and want a human, community-based differentiator alongside your AI and automation investments.
steps: Treat this as a counter-position to AI perfection: the source argues flawless automated service will become boring and stop being a differentiator, so invest in what machines can't provide.

Design a community around a shared customer activity or identity rather than around your products, following examples the source cites: Lululemon's workout lifestyle community and Nike's running clubs.
Use physical or real-time gatherings where feasible, since the source frames the value as real belonging in response to more virtual relationships.
Give the community a reason to exist independent of discounts — training, events, peer advice, shared goals — so it isn't just a loyalty wrapper.
Connect the community to your ecommerce operations: member perks, early access, UGC that feeds reviews and product discovery.
Measure belonging through participation and repeat purchase behavior rather than membership counts alone.
caveats: The source attributes the differentiation claim to the Lululemon and Nike examples; it is a prediction, not a measured outcome.
Community programs are operationally heavy and may not fit every product category.

cards.title: Make brand content deliberately unpolished to signal a human wrote it
cards.summary: As audiences learn to spot and discount AI-generated polish, slightly imperfect, human-written copy increasingly earns attention and trust — the source calls this 'un-AI-fication'.
cards.use_when: You are writing product descriptions, post-purchase emails, or brand content and deciding how much polish to apply versus keeping human texture.
steps: Identify content where trust matters most — founder notes, brand story, support replies, product copy with a strong voice — and protect those from heavy AI polish.
Allow minor imperfections: less sterile phrasing, small errors, real opinions; the source argues people notice polish and disengage, doubting the content is real.
Keep a human in the loop for tone on relationship-building touchpoints rather than letting AI write first-draft-and-publish.
Test human-textured copy against polished copy in email and landing pages and watch engagement and response, not just open rates.
Use AI for structure, research and drafts, then edit toward your brand's voice rather than sanding everything smooth.
Keep this consistent with brand-agent voice work so all AI-assisted communication sounds like your brand, not a generic assistant.
caveats: The source presents this as an emerging trend; there is no measured performance data behind the claim that imperfect copy outperforms.
Deliberate errors must not bleed into factual product information, pricing or policy where accuracy is required.

cards.title: Build brand agents with a distinctive voice instead of generic AI bots
cards.summary: Generic AI bots will sound identical and forgettable, so the source urges companies to build 'brand agents' that embody the company's unique voice and tone.
cards.use_when: You are deploying a customer-service chatbot or shopping assistant and need to decide how much investment goes into voice and brand personality versus pure functionality.
steps: Before writing dialogue flows, define the brand's voice in concrete terms (tone, vocabulary, pacing, what the brand would never say) and use it as the spec for the agent.

Draft sample conversations and have people familiar with the brand judge whether the agent is recognizably your brand, testing the source's bar: users should know they're talking to your brand, like Apple, Disney or Lego agents.
Match personality to the use case: a pragmatic, calm voice for a logistics brand versus an energetic one for a fitness brand, rather than one generic helpful-assistant tone.
Protect voice through every update so it doesn't flatten back to generic chatbot phrasing as the system scales.
Warn stakeholders that defaulting to off-the-shelf technology, as the source puts it, flattens your differentiating brand aspect.
Monitor voice consistency alongside resolution and conversion metrics, and review transcripts regularly for drift.
caveats: This is the source's forward-looking argument, not a benchmarked outcome; brand voice has no standard metric.
A strongly voiced agent still requires accurate information and reliable resolution to be useful.

input.source_name: 9 Customer Experience Trends for 2026 by Steven Van Belleghem.docx
input.text:
05-SET / store setup and tech Goes here. A predictive video on the 2026 trends for customer experience (CX), specifically focusing on how Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) will fundamentally alter consumer search behavior, go-to-market strategies, and post-purchase support. Not here. • Paid ad campaign strategies or ROAS tracking -> 06-MEA • Organic social media content planning -> 13-ORG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details the technological shift toward AI-agent-driven e-commerce, algorithmic visibility, and the transformation of customer service from a cost center to a profit center using hyperpersonalization and brand agents. modules: [SET] topics: [artificial intelligence, customer experience, LLMs, AI agents, algorithmic invisibility, hyperpersonalization, customer service, brand agents, future trends 2026] tier: 3 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. AI search behavior / predicting that consumers will shift from traditional search engines to AI platforms, utilizing autonomous "agents" to perform automated tasks (e.g., automatically canceling and rebooking a flight if the price drops while sleeping); go-to-market shifts / explaining how the entire marketing and sales funnel will collapse into a single AI platform, requiring a complete overhaul of traditional digital marketing strategies; algorithmic invisibility / the critical new challenge of ensuring an e-commerce brand is recommended by LLMs (like ChatGPT or Perplexity) during unbranded queries, highlighting that third-party customer reviews are the strongest ranking signal; customer service profitability / predicting that AI-driven automation will drive the cost-per-contact to near zero, while hyperpersonalized upselling during support interactions will turn traditional customer service cost centers into profit centers; hyperpersonalization / moving beyond basic marketing personalization to creating custom AI "coaches" (e.g., L'Oreal's beauty assistant) that provide 24/7 personalized value to the consumer; emotional AI / utilizing AI not just for operational efficiency, but to create emotional bonds, companionship, and delight (e.g., smart glasses with automated subtitles for the deaf); belonging as a service / forecasting that as AI perfection becomes a boring commodity, brands that facilitate physical, human communities (like Lululemon) will differentiate themselves; un-AI-fication / the counter-trend where unpolished, human-written content with minor mistakes will command higher attention and trust than perfectly polished, AI-generated text; brand agents / the necessity of moving away from generic AI bots to developing customized "brand agents" that strictly embody the unique voice and tone of the company.

Look for.

Algorithmic Invisibility: The concept that the new SEO is optimizing for LLM recommendations (like ChatGPT), where third-party customer reviews and organic mentions are the primary drivers of visibility.

Zero-Effort Consumer Agents: The prediction that consumers will deploy personal AI agents to autonomously hunt for deals and execute purchases in the background, putting massive downward pressure on e-commerce pricing.

Customer Service as a Profit Center: The shift where AI reduces the operational cost-per-contact to zero while simultaneously enabling highly accurate, context-aware cross-selling during support interactions.

Un-AI-fication: The emerging trend where slightly flawed, unpolished copy will perform better because consumers will instinctively trust it as human-generated over perfectly sterile AI copy.

Skip. General philosophical musings about the future of humanity and AI companionship unless tied directly to a brand strategy.

Scope mix. 100% growth (predictive technology trends and advanced AI strategy). Volume. ~400 words.
